title: Brussels sprout, parsnip and split pea soup

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything here is a whole food or a cupboard staple: vegetables, split peas, stock, wholegrain mustard, oil and lemon.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one large pan, a knife and a board, and the technique is simple simmering.

works.reason: 200g split peas in 1.5 litres of stock with parsnips and 500g sprouts makes a hearty chunky soup for four, and adding the sprouts at the end keeps them from going grey.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes of active work covers chopping the onion, garlic and parsnips, slicing 500g of sprouts and softening the onion, and 55 minutes of cooking matches the 45-minute simmer plus the sprouts.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme and lemon, is used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears, and 'yellow split peas' matches its id.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming pulse soup suits mid-February, and 500g of sprouts makes them the main vegetable rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no fuss or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Split peas and plenty of vegetables make a filling, nourishing lunch that a family would happily eat again.
